translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty saw through their guilt; because the palace compilation projects were unfinished, you merely relieved them of office and kept them on to edit books—a mercy that went to the utmost!

sentences.zh: 士奇不思改過自新，仍怙惡不悛，當聖駕南巡，上諭嚴戒餽送，以軍法治罪。

translations.literal: Shiqi did not think to reform and renew himself, still relied on evil without repentance; when the sacred chariot toured south, the Emperor instructed strict prohibition of gifts, with military law to punish crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi did not repent or reform. He persisted in his wickedness. When Your Majesty made the southern tour, you decreed a strict ban on gifts, with military law for offenders.

sentences.zh: 惟士奇與鴻緒愍不畏死，鴻緒在淮、揚等處，招攬各官餽送萬金，潛遺士奇。

translations.literal: Only Shiqi and Hongxu, heedless and not fearing death; Hongxu in Huai and Yang and other places recruited all officials' gifts of ten thousand gold, secretly sent to Shiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shiqi and Hongxu still defied the prohibition without fear of death. In Huai, Yang, and other regions Hongxu solicited gifts of ten thousand taels from officials and secretly forwarded them to Shiqi.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚如此，他處可知。

translations.literal: Huai and Yang thus—other places can be known.
translations.idiomatic: If this was done in Huai and Yang, the rest may be imagined.

sentences.zh: 是士奇等欺君滅法，背公行私，其罪之可誅者四也。

translations.literal: Thus Shiqi and the rest deceived the ruler and extinguished the law, turned their backs on the public and practiced the private—the fourth of their crimes that deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they deceived the throne and nullified the law, betraying the public good for private gain—the fourth count deserving punishment.

sentences.zh: 王鴻緒、陳元龍鼎甲出身，儼然士林翹楚；

translations.literal: Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong—chief graduates in origin, augustly the forest of letters' lofty pinnacles;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongxu and Chen Yuanlong had risen as palace graduates and stood among the foremost scholars of the realm;

sentences.zh: 竟不顧淸議，依媚大臣，無所不至。

translations.literal: Yet did not care for pure criticism, leaned and fawned on great ministers, nothing they did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: yet they spurned public opinion and fawned upon great ministers to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 苟圖富貴，傷敗名教，豈不玷朝班而羞當世之士哉？

translations.literal: If only seeking wealth and rank, injuring and destroying the teaching of names—does this not stain the court ranks and shame the men of the age?
translations.idiomatic: To grasp at riches and rank while trampling the norms of propriety—does this not dishonor the court and shame the scholars of the age?

sentences.zh: 總之髙士奇、王鴻緒、陳元龍、何楷、王頊齡等，豺狼其性，蛇蠍其心，鬼蜮其形。

translations.literal: In sum Gao Shiqi, Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong, He Kai, Wang Songling, and the rest—wolves and dogs their nature, serpents and scorpions their heart, demons and sprites their form.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, Gao Shiqi, Wang Hongxu, Chen Yuanlong, He Kai, Wang Songling, and the rest have the nature of wolves, hearts of scorpions, and faces of ogres.

sentences.zh: 畏勢者既觀望而不敢言，趨勢者-{復}-擁戴而不肯言。

translations.literal: Those who fear power already look on and dare not speak; those who court power again rally and support and are unwilling to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fear power hold their tongues and watch from the sidelines; those who court power rally to them and will not speak out.

sentences.zh: 臣若不言，有負聖恩。

translations.literal: If your servant does not speak, he has failed the sacred grace.
translations.idiomatic: If I remain silent, I fail Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 故不避嫌怨，請立賜罷斥，明正典刑，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Therefore not avoiding suspicion and resentment, I request forthwith to be granted dismissal and expulsion, clearly to rectify by the statutes—great fortune for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, heedless of enmity, I beg that they be dismissed at once and punished according to law, to the great good of the realm."

sentences.zh: 疎入，士奇等倶休致回籍。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Shiqi and the rest all retired on leave and returned to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, Shiqi and the others were all allowed to retire and return to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 副都-{御}-史許三禮复疎劾解任尚書徐-{乾}-學與士奇姻親，招搖納賄，相爲表裡。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Sanli again memorialized impeaching the relieved Minister Xu Qianxue as marriage kin with Shiqi, swaggering and receiving bribes, mutually acting as outside and inside.
translations.idiomatic: The vice censor-in-chief Xu Sanli submitted a further memorial impeaching the retired minister Xu Qianxue, who was related to Shiqi by marriage, for taking bribes and colluding with him as partners inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 部議以所劾無據，得寢。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated that the impeached matters had no evidence; the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that the charges lacked evidence, and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，召來京修書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, he was summoned to the capital to edit books.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of the Kangxi reign, he was recalled to the capital to work on the compilation.

sentences.zh: 士奇既至，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: Shiqi having arrived, still attended directly at the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqi arrived, he again served on duty in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，以養母乞歸，詔允之，特授詹事府詹事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, on grounds of nourishing his mother he begged to return; an edict approved it, and he was specially made Junior Tutor of the Mansion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he asked leave to return home to care for his mother. The emperor granted it and specially appointed him junior tutor in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 尋擢禮部侍郎，以母老未赴。

translations.literal: Soon promoted Vice Minister of Rites; because his mother was old he did not go to assume office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of rites but did not take up the post because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，士奇迎駕淮安，扈蹕至杭州。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when the Emperor made a southern tour, Shiqi welcomed the imperial carriage at Huai'an and escorted the retinue to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, when the emperor toured the south, Shiqi met the imperial procession at Huai'an and accompanied it to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及回鑾，-{復}-從至京師，屢入對，賜予優渥。

translations.literal: When the imperial chariot returned, again followed to the capital, repeatedly entered for audience, gifts and favors generous and thick.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor turned homeward, Shiqi again accompanied him to the capital, was received in audience many times, and was granted lavish favors.

sentences.zh: 上顧侍臣曰：「朕初讀書，内監授以四子本經，作時文；

translations.literal: The Emperor looked at the attending ministers and said: "When I first studied, the eunuchs taught me the Four Books text in the original, to compose examination essays;
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants the emperor said: "When I first began to study, eunuchs taught me the Four Books in their original text, so I could write examination essays.

sentences.zh: 得士奇，始知學問門徑。

translations.literal: Having obtained Shiqi, I then knew the entrance to scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: It was only when I found Shiqi that I learned the true approach to learning.

sentences.zh: 初見士奇得古人詩文，一覽即知其時代，心以爲異，未-{幾}-，朕亦能之。

translations.literal: At first seeing Shiqi obtain ancient men's poetry and prose, one glance and he knew their period; in the heart taking it strange—not long, I too could do it.
translations.idiomatic: When I first saw Shiqi take up a piece of ancient poetry or prose and identify its period at a glance, I marveled at it; before long I could do the same myself.

sentences.zh: 士奇無戰陣功，而朕待之厚，以其裨朕學問者大也。」

translations.literal: Shiqi has no battle-array achievements, yet I treat him thickly, because his benefit to my learning is great."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi won no laurels in war, yet I have treated him generously because he has done so much to advance my scholarship.

sentences.zh: 尋遣歸，是年卒-{於}-家。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent home; that year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent home, and that same year he died there.

sentences.zh: 上深惜之，命加給全葬，授其子庶吉士輿爲編修。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply regretted it, ordered added grants for a full funeral, and appointed his son, the Hanlin bachelor Yu, as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply, ordered a full state funeral subsidy, and appointed his son Yu, then a Hanlin bachelor, as compiler.

sentences.zh: 尋諡文恪。

translations.literal: Soon posthumous title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the posthumous name Wenke.

sentences.zh: 論曰：儒臣直内廷，謂之「書房」，存未入關前舊名也。

translations.literal: The historian comments: Confucian officials attending directly in the inner court are called "study rooms," preserving the old name from before entering the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The historians observe: Scholar-officials who served directly in the inner court were called "study rooms," preserving the pre-conquest nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 上書房授諸皇子讀，尊爲師傅；

translations.literal: The Upper Study instructs the imperial sons in reading, honored as masters;
translations.idiomatic: The Upper Study instructed the princes and was held in honor as their masters;

sentences.zh: 南書房以詩文書畫供-{禦}-，地分淸切，參與密勿。

translations.literal: The Southern Study with poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting supplies the imperial—rank divided pure and urgent, participates in intimate counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Study supplied poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting for the emperor's use. Its station was eminent and close; its members took part in confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學、士奇先-{後}-入直，鴻緒亦以文學進。

translations.literal: Qianxue and Shiqi first and after entered direct attendance; Hongxu also advanced by literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue and Shiqi entered service in turn; Hongxu also rose through literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 乃憑藉權勢，互結黨援，納賄營私，致屢遭彈劾，聖祖-{曲}-予保全。

translations.literal: Yet relying on power and influence, mutually forming factional support, receiving bribes and pursuing private gain, thereby frequently suffering impeachment—the Kangxi Emperor bent to spare and preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they leaned on power, formed factions, accepted bribes, and pursued private gain, and were impeached again and again; the Kangxi Emperor bent the law to preserve them.

sentences.zh: -{乾}-學、鴻緒猶得以書局自隨，竟編纂之業，士奇亦以恩禮終，不其幸歟！

translations.literal: Qianxue and Hongxu still could take the book bureau with them, finishing the work of compilation; Shiqi also ended with favor and ritual—was it not their fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue and Hongxu were still allowed to keep their place at the compilation bureau and finish their editorial work; Shiqi too died with imperial favor intact—is this not extraordinary fortune?
